ladder.teaches: recursive DFS that returns a value (depth, size)
ladder.why: A node's answer is built from its children's answers: depth = 1 + max(left, right), with 0 for an empty tree.

ladder.teaches: DFS that passes state down (path sums)
ladder.why: Information can flow down instead of up: carry the remaining target into each child and check it only at a leaf.
BFS with a queue, processed one whole level per round by fixing the queue's length first.

ladder.teaches: post-order: combine the children's answers (diameter, balanced)
ladder.why: Return one thing (height) to the parent while scoring another (left height + right height) at every node.

ladder.teaches: post-order: combine the children's answers (diameter, balanced)
ladder.why: Compute heights bottom-up once and check each node on the way, instead of recomputing heights top-down in O(n^2).
Level-order BFS where you keep only the last node of each level.

ladder.teaches: DFS that passes state down (path sums)
ladder.why: Pass the whole path down to each child and emit it at a leaf, recursively or with an explicit stack that keeps left-to-right order.
Preorder names the root, inorder splits the rest into left and right subtrees; an index map makes the rebuild O(n).

ladder.teaches: recursive DFS that returns a value (depth, size)
ladder.why: An OA story that is really subtree size: each boss's count is the sum of their reports' subtree sizes.

ladder.teaches: post-order: combine the children's answers (diameter, balanced)
ladder.why: Subtree sizes computed post-order on an n-ary adjacency list, then a check at each node using its children's sizes.

ladder.teaches: recursive DFS that returns a value (depth, size)
ladder.why: A left-before-right DFS emits the leaves in order; collect them for two trees and compare.
BFS levels give each level's total; each node's cousins are the level total minus its sibling group.

ladder.teaches: recursive DFS that returns a value (depth, size)
ladder.why: The propagation order is a preorder DFS, and each subtree is a contiguous block of it of length size[v].

ladder.teaches: post-order: combine the children's answers (diameter, balanced)
ladder.why: The diameter pattern with weights: offer the parent max(0, best downward gain) and score the bend using both sides.

ladder.teaches: post-order: combine the children's answers (diameter, balanced)
ladder.why: Same post-order shape, but both ends must be real leaves, so negative branches cannot be dropped and only two-child nodes can bend the path.

notes: Most classic binary-tree problems were in no pool and were taken from the free bank (max depth, diameter, balanced, right side view, root-to-leaf paths, build from preorder+inorder, leaf-to-leaf sum). 'Build a tree from traversals' has one rung; morgan-stanley-binary-tree-codec (serialize/deserialize) would be a natural extra. amazon-amount-of-time-to-infect-binary-tree was left out: it is a general edge-list tree and teaches graph BFS more than tree DFS.
